concept.name: How to Prepare for Low-Level Design (LLD)

spark.title: How to Prepare for Low-Level Design (LLD)
spark.summary: Excel in Low-Level Design rounds by translating ambiguous product rules into clean OOP interfaces, SOLID/GoF patterns, thread-safe state transitions, and testable Java/Python code.
spark.keyTakeaway: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, start with entities, invariants, and interfaces—not giant inheritance trees—and proactively handle concurrency (locks, CAS, idempotency) and extensibility.
spark.byteSummary:
Excel in Low-Level Design rounds by translating ambiguous product rules into clean OOP interfaces, SOLID/GoF patterns, thread-safe state transitions, and testable Java/Python code.

LLD interviews evaluate whether your code stays maintainable as requirements evolve mid-interview (e.g., adding a new pricing rule, eviction policy, or vehicle type).

Start with entities, invariants, and interfaces—not giant inheritance trees—and proactively handle concurrency (locks, CAS, idempotency) and extensibility.

concept.whyItMatters: LLD interviews evaluate whether your code stays maintainable as requirements evolve mid-interview (e.g., adding a new pricing rule, eviction policy, or vehicle type). Applying [SOLID principles](/concept/design-principles-solid), [Strategy/Factory/Observer patterns](/concept/design-patterns-gof), and explicit [concurrency control](/concept/optimistic-concurrency-control) separates senior engineers from candidates who write monolithic `if/else` blocks.
whenToUse: 45–60 minute Machine Coding or LLD rounds (LRU Cache, Parking Lot, Elevator, Splitwise, Ticket Booking, Rate Limiter).
whenNotToUse: Over-engineering 12 abstract factories before confirming the core 3–4 classes and use cases.
keyPoints: Step 1 (Clarify Entities & Use Cases): List core actors, state transitions, and edge cases (e.g., double-booking, concurrent eviction).
Step 2 (Interfaces & Composition over Inheritance): Use Strategy for swappable policies (eviction, pricing, allocation) and Repository interfaces for storage.
Step 3 (Concurrency & Thread Safety): Explicitly identify shared mutable state and guard it with fine-grained locks, `ConcurrentHashMap`, or atomic CAS.
Step 4 (Clean Runnable Code & Tests): Write clean, compile-ready Java or Python with happy-path and concurrency/edge-case tests.

sections.content:
## Preparation & Execution Matrix

| LLD Focus Area | What Interviewers Look For | Example Pattern |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Modularity** | Small cohesive classes, single responsibility | Service + Repository + Domain Model |
| **Extensibility** | Add new rule without editing core engine | Strategy / State / Factory |
| **Concurrency** | Zero race conditions on shared state | Striped locks, `ReentrantLock`, CAS |
| **Edge Cases** | Nulls, capacity=0, duplicate requests | Guard clauses + `IllegalStateException` |

steps.title: Normal Path
steps.explanation: Caller sends work to Router / API (Normal Path).

steps.title: Core Execution
steps.explanation: Router / API coordinates with Processor while preserving the core invariant (Core Execution).

steps.title: Contention / Fault
steps.explanation: Under load skew or dependency lag, State Layer absorbs pressure without cascading (Contention / Fault).

steps.title: Steady Convergence
steps.explanation: The system stabilizes cleanly within its latency and correctness budget (Steady Convergence).

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement How To Prepare For Lld without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, start with entities, invariants, and interfaces—not giant inheritance trees—and proactively handle concurrency (locks, CAS, idempotency) and extensibility.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When How To Prepare For Lld experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.
